correctness.rationale: The four sectors follow from the standard representation tensor-square decomposition. Eigenvalues are derived via fixed-point covariance and symmetric/skew trace identities. For n=5 and 6 the five classwise dual differences are nonnegative rational numbers; for n>=7 they are explicit positive polynomials divided by positive polynomials. Each candidate probability law yields matching positive eigenvalues, so the lower bounds are tight. Independent finite enumeration of five complete classes in n=4,5,6 passed.

value.rationale: Short-motion perturbations are a natural sparsity constraint for sampling rank data. The theorem determines exact best possible stability on the entire irreducible standard Fourier block under all class-invariant sampling laws, proves uniqueness of a tight dimension as a consequence of strict lower bounds for n>=5, provides rational optimal samplers, and establishes exact cubic high-rank growth.
